definitions.explanation: The basic verb for dying. Can be used for people, animals, or plants. In polite contexts, 亡くなる (nakunaru) is often preferred when speaking about people.

examples.japanese: その{犬|いぬ}は{去年|きょねん}{死|し}にました。
{花|はな}が{死|し}んでしまった。
{祖父|そふ}は{十年前|じゅうねんまえ}に{死|し}にました。
examples.english: My grandfather died ten years ago.
examples.notes: In more polite speech, 亡くなりました would be used

notes: 死ぬ is one of the few godan verbs ending in ぬ. Its conjugation is unique: 死なない (negative), 死にます (polite), 死んだ (past). Note the past tense uses んだ, not にた. In polite company, especially when talking about recently deceased people, the euphemism 亡くなる (nakunaru) is preferred.
